headline_seed: U.S.-Iran Updates: Trump says Iran to "get a beating" as war expands with U.S.-Saudi strikes in Iraq - CBS News

consensus_facts: On Tuesday, July 28, 2026, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps launched multiple ballistic missiles at U.S. forces in the Middle East, which CENTCOM described as an 'attempted surprise attack'; CENTCOM said all missiles were intercepted (Axios, CBS News, CNN, ABC News).
Jordan's military said it intercepted five Iranian missiles early Wednesday (CBS News, CNN).

U.S. and Saudi Arabian forces conducted joint strikes on Iran-aligned forces in Iraq in response to Iranian drone attacks, described by CENTCOM as more than 30 IRGC-directed drone attacks over the previous 72 hours (Axios, CBS News, CNN).
The Iran-backed Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) said at least 20 of its fighters were killed in the U.S.-Saudi strikes in Iraq (CBS News, CNN).

On Wednesday, July 29, President Trump told reporters in the Oval Office, 'We're going to be hitting them very hard because it's our turn to hit them. They know it's coming' (CBS News, CNN, ABC News).
The U.S. began launching a new round of strikes on Iran around 8 p.m. ET Wednesday, which CENTCOM called 'a powerful response' to Iran's attempted attacks on U.S. forces (CBS News, CNN, ABC News).
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu met with President Trump at the White House on Tuesday for talks focused heavily on Iran (Axios, CBS News, Al Jazeera, CNN).
Vessel traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains far below prewar levels, with prewar averages of roughly 100-120 crossings per day (CBS News, CNN).
CENTCOM cited more than 600 attempted attacks on U.S. citizens and facilities in Iraq by Iran-aligned militias between February and April (Axios, CBS News).

disagreements.topic: Casualty count in U.S.-Saudi strikes in Iraq

positions.CBS News: PMF said at least 20 fighters killed and 32 wounded; earlier AFP-sourced report cited at least 10 dead
positions.CNN: PMF said at least 20 killed; a provincial Iranian official said four IRGC members killed providing Arbaeen pilgrimage security; PMF spokesman told CNN six Iranian pilgrims were killed

disagreements.topic: Number of ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz

positions.CBS News: Cites Kpler that transits remain extremely limited; CENTCOM redirected 20 commercial ships evading its blockade, up from 12
positions.CNN: MarineTraffic data shows at least 14 commercial ships passed through in the last 24 hours vs. ~120/day before the war
positions.CNN (July 27): Fewer than 10 commodity ships passed as of Monday morning vs. ~100/day before the war

positions.Al Jazeera: Oil prices fell to lowest level in over a week on Monday July 27; Brent fell 8.7% to $88.36
positions.CNN (July 27): Brent fell 11.3% to $85.87, biggest decline since April 8
positions.CNN (July 29): Oil prices rose in the wake of renewed fighting

positions.Al Jazeera: Trump said 'we are having good talks' with Iran but not interested in prolonged negotiations
positions.Axios: Trump said U.S. in 'very deep talks' with Iran, warned of return to 'very strong military action' if diplomacy failed
positions.CNN (July 27): Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Baghaei said there are 'no negotiations with the United States at present'

positions.CBS News / CNN / ABC News: Quote Trump's Oval Office line 'hitting them very hard'
positions.CNN: Additionally reports Trump told Fox News 'We are going to beat the f**king sh*t out of them'

framing_analysis.CBS News: Two live-blog entries anchor coverage in CENTCOM statements and blockade/sanctions mechanics. Leads on the new round of U.S. strikes and Trump's 'hitting them very hard' quote, then details State Department sanctions on Hormuz 'insurance' schemes and shadow-fleet vessels. Includes the Egyptian port drone strike as a potential widening of the conflict and folds in a Federal Reserve rate decision tied to war-driven energy costs. Neutral, wire-heavy tone; casualty reporting attributed carefully to PMF and AFP.
framing_analysis.Al Jazeera English: Frames the conflict as 'the US and Israel's war on Iran,' foregrounding Israeli actions in Gaza and the occupied West Bank, UN condemnation of settlements, and possible Israeli war crimes in Lebanon alongside the Iran strikes. Emphasizes regional and Global South context, oil price declines, and diplomatic framing ('good talks'). Gives more weight to Iranian and third-party perspectives than the U.S. outlets.
framing_analysis.Axios: Tight, single-event focus on Iran's ballistic missile attack on a U.S. base in Jordan as the first since Trump's pause. 'Why it matters' framing stresses the threat to the fragile diplomatic pause and Trump's decision point. Prominently quotes Trump's 'very deep talks'/'very strong military action' warning and the earlier July attack that killed two U.S. service members. Much of the retrieved text is cookie/consent boilerplate.
framing_analysis.CNN: Leads with 'Trump says Iran going to get a beating' and the fresh U.S. strikes, emphasizing explosions reported by Iranian state media Press TV. Notably includes Trump's profane Fox News quote and his warning to China's Xi over arming Tehran. Provides the most granular casualty breakdown (four IRGC members, six pilgrims) and detailed shipping-lane data for both Hormuz and Bab al-Mandeb. Frames the Iranian missile attack as a departure from the tit-for-tat pattern.
framing_analysis.ABC News: Sparse entry that provides the deepest historical framing: dates the war's start to Feb. 28 with joint U.S.-Israeli strikes, and notes June negotiations toward a war-ending deal based on a signed memorandum of understanding. Emphasizes the Strait of Hormuz as the primary flashpoint and reports the Trump-Netanyahu meeting weighed military, diplomatic, and economic options, with Netanyahu stating no preference.

primary_source_alignment: No primary source documents were located for this story. CENTCOM statements are quoted secondhand through multiple outlets but the underlying releases were not provided in the dossier; direct alignment against primary text could not be performed.
missing_context: No outlet independently verified CENTCOM's claim that all Iranian missiles were intercepted; the claim originates from a single U.S. military source repeated across outlets.

Casualty figures for the Iraq strikes come entirely from the Iran-backed PMF, a provincial Iranian official, and AFP-cited sources; no independent or Iraqi government confirmation is provided, and figures were labeled preliminary.
The identity of the party responsible for the Egyptian port drone strikes at Damietta was not confirmed by any outlet.
No outlet clarified how many total Iranian missiles were fired at the Jordan base versus the five Jordan reported intercepting, leaving the scale of the attack ambiguous.
Casualty figures, if any, from the U.S. strikes on Iran itself (the 8 p.m. ET Wednesday round and prior campaign) are not reported in any article.
The current legal or diplomatic status of the June memorandum of understanding referenced by ABC News is not updated in the later dossier articles.
No primary CENTCOM press release, sanctions designation text, or shipping-data source was included in the dossier for direct verification.
brief.suggested_post_type_reason: Multiple outlets reported the same escalation with materially different emphasis — Al Jazeera centers an Israeli war on Iran, CNN foregrounds Trump's profane vow and China warning, ABC supplies the historical frame — and key figures (casualties, shipping transits, oil prices) diverge across sources, making this a coverage-comparison story rather than a straight report.
